final_recommendation: The room converged on a forced merger with UBS over the weekend as the primary path, with Swiss government providing a loss protection guarantee (CHF 8-12bn range) and SNB liquidity backstop (CHF 100bn+), to be announced Sunday evening before Asian markets open.
minority_objections: Concern that temporary nationalization carries unacceptable contagion risk to Switzerland's wealth management credibility
Fear that AT1 write-down while preserving equity value will trigger massive litigation and set bad precedent for Swiss financial instruments
key_conflicts: FINMA wants AT1 write-down to clean balance sheet vs Federal Council fears legal/political blowback
SNB wants government to provide loss guarantees vs Federal Council wants SNB to bear more risk via liquidity only
UBS demands maximum subsidies and full tail-risk protection vs Federal Council cannot be seen repeating 2008 bailout
AT1 bondholders expect equity wiped first per normal hierarchy vs FINMA/acquirer preference for AT1 write-down under viability-event language
key_concessions: Federal Council accepts CHF 8-10bn loss guarantee structured as 'insurance' to secure UBS participation
SNB provides CHF 100bn+ liquidity facility, accepting some may never be repaid
FINMA accepts equity holders retain some value despite being 'unfair' vs AT1 to get deal done
UBS pays token amount (CHF 2-4bn, 60-80% discount) and accepts reputational risk as 'bailout beneficiary'
Credit Suisse board/management resign and accept immediate termination
red_lines: FINMA will not allow Credit Suisse to open Monday without credible rescue
SNB will not allow disorderly collapse that threatens Swiss franc credibility
Federal Council cannot be seen as repeating 2008 UBS bailout (politically toxic)
UBS will not proceed without government absorbing tail risks (litigation, legacy positions, client defections)
Wealth clients cannot tolerate any asset freeze, even temporary
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Integration costs of CHF 5-10bn over 3-5 years mentioned but not deeply analyzed for feasibility
UBS internal board conflict (CEO may favor empire building but board fears integration risk) noted but not war-gamed
International regulatory approval timing treated as manageable via emergency consultations, but execution risk underweighted
Hedge fund AT1 holders' litigation strategy and injunction timing not fully mapped
downstream_risk_variables: Actual weekend client flight volume (threshold: CHF 20-30bn triggers deal abandonment)
UBS board's final loss guarantee demand vs Federal Council's political pain threshold
AT1 legal opinion strength and speed of injunction filings
Top 50 UHNW client retention rate after Sunday outreach calls
Asian market reaction Monday morning if announcement timing slips or messaging fails
uncertainty_notes: The AT1 treatment decision remains the critical unresolved fork: write-down (cleaner for acquirer, massive litigation) vs preservation with haircut (higher government cost, avoids precedent problem). UBS's actual willingness to proceed and minimum acceptable terms are unknown until weekend negotiations. The 15% tail risk of emergency nationalization if UBS walks is acknowledged but the operational readiness of that Plan B is unclear.
